content: Artesunate suppositories are utilized in the treatment of malaria. Artesunate is a water-soluble antimalarial compound derived from dihydroartemisinin. Artemisinins, the class of compounds to which artesunate belongs, are sesquiterpene lactones extracted from Artemisia annua, a plant traditionally used in Chinese medicine. The mortality risk associated with severe malaria is significantly influenced by the delay between the onset of symptoms and the initiation of treatment. Therefore, rapid access to effective treatment is critical. In many cases, patients with severe malaria may experience symptoms such as vomiting, seizures, or coma, which can make oral administration of medication impractical. Additionally, healthcare facilities capable of providing alternative non-oral treatments are often inaccessible in remote areas. Artesunate, when administered in suppository form, offers a potential solution to this challenge. It can be deployed in remote regions and administered promptly at the onset of symptoms, thereby improving outcomes. Artesunate is one of several artemisinin derivatives that were discovered and developed by Chinese scientists and officially registered in China during the 1980s. Since the 1990s, the UNICEF/UNDP/World Bank/WHO Special Programme for Research and Training in Tropical Diseases (TDR) has supported studies to evaluate the properties of this drug. Early evidence suggested that artesunate, when administered rectally, was effective in treating severe malaria. Significant research on artemisinin suppositories for severe malaria was conducted in Vietnam during the early 1990s. Clinical trials involving rectal artesunate followed by mefloquine treatment for moderately severe malaria were subsequently carried out in Thailand. These studies provided valuable insights into the efficacy and potential applications of rectal artesunate in managing malaria.
